current_p1_ru: Product Manager, Software Developer, UX Designer, Game Developer. Ты в продуктовой технологической команде. Не «обслуживаешь IT» — а строишь продукт.
current_p1_en:
Product Manager, Software Developer, UX Designer, Game Developer. You're on a product tech team. Not serving IT from the side — building the product itself.
Why it works: you have both technical and product thinking. You can dig into code and still think about the user.
Some people are surprised: "you have both?". Both. And that combination is exactly what people pay for.
What's worth knowing: tech roles require constant learning. What was current 3 years ago is outdated now. Stay current, or your salary stops growing.

current_p1_ru: Graphic Designer, Content Creator, Photographer, Filmmaker. Ты в визуальном креативе. Создаёшь контент, который видят люди.
current_p1_en:
Graphic Designer, Content Creator, Photographer, Filmmaker. You belong in visual creative work: making things people actually see.
It lands because you have an artistic eye and technical execution. Most have only one; you combine.
You may hear people don't believe: "you're not at a big studio". You don't need to be. You have your clients and your style.
What's worth knowing: creative professions often get overpaid at the start and underpaid later. Learn to raise prices. And invest in portfolio — it works for you 24/7.

current_p1_ru: Writer, Journalist, Musician, Artist. Ты творец смысла. Не «делаешь продукт»; создаёшь произведение — текст, песню, картину, материал.
current_p1_en:
Writer, Journalist, Musician, Artist. You make meaning. Not "making a product"; creating a work — text, song, painting, story.
The logic is simple: you have a deep inner life. Most people live reactively; you live to express.
People sometimes say: "you can't make money on this". Maybe. Maybe. But you are not in it only for money. You are in it for voice.
What's worth knowing: creative professions are also serious economic risk. Learn to combine with more stable income. Many great writers worked as editors all their lives so they could afford to write.

current_p1_ru: Data Analyst, Marketing Manager, Investment Banker, Consultant. Ты работаешь с цифрами и стратегиями. Анализ, фреймворки, рекомендации — это твоё.
current_p1_en:
Data Analyst, Marketing Manager, Investment Banker, Consultant. You work with numbers and strategies. Analysis, frameworks, recommendations — yours.
This fits because you have a structured mind. Work without clear metrics bores you; you need something measurable.
Some people are surprised: "you live in Excel?". In Excel and PowerPoint — and you are comfortable there.
What's worth knowing: these professions are high return, high load. Hours often go off the chart. Learn to defend boundaries. If you work 70 hours a week for years — burnout is inevitable.

current_p1_ru: Founder, Content Creator, Sales Rep, Investment Banker. Тебе нужен риск как часть профессии. Не «стабильная зарплата»; а большой потенциал и большая возможность провала.
current_p1_en:
Founder, Content Creator, Sales Rep, Investment Banker. You need risk as part of your profession. Not "stable salary"; big upside and big possibility of failure.
Why it works: you have a strong appetite for achievement. Without risk you're bored; you need every day to be a bet.
You may hear people worry: "and if it doesn't work out?". Maybe it won't. Then the next thing might. You are not the type to freeze after failure.
What's worth knowing: risk professions are emotional swings. Today on top, tomorrow in a hole. Learn not to identify with short-term outcomes. Otherwise your self-esteem rides the same swings, and that's exhausting.

current_p1_ru: Doctor, Therapist, Teacher, HR Specialist. Ты в помогающей профессии. Твоя работа — это люди и их состояния, и ты в этом находишь смысл.
current_p1_en:
Doctor, Therapist, Teacher, HR Specialist. You're in a helping profession. Your work is people and their inner states, and you find meaning in it.
It lands because you have empathy as a resource. Most people burn out from others' problems; you have the capacity to hold them.
People sometimes are surprised: "how do you handle it?". You handle it. It feels like a calling, and the capacity is there.
What's worth knowing: helping professions are #1 for burnout. Without supervision, personal therapy, rest — you'll burn out in 10 years. Self-care is part of professionalism here, not "weakness".

current_p1_ru: Engineer, Architect, Researcher, Pilot. Ты в профессии, требующей точности. Здесь нет «приблизительно» — есть «правильно» и «неправильно».
current_p1_en:
Engineer, Architect, Researcher, Pilot. You're in a profession that requires precision. There's no "approximately" — there's "right" and "wrong".
The logic is simple: you have an engineer's mind. Work with vague results bores you; you need something concrete at the end.
Some people are surprised: "you're a pedant". Pedant. But my pedantry saves lives / builds buildings / advances science.
What's worth knowing: precise professions are often slow in progress. One project can take years. Learn to accept long horizons. Without that patience you'll feel "stagnant".

current_p1_ru: Lawyer, Journalist, Sales Rep, PR Specialist. Твой инструмент — слово. Ты убеждаешь, продаёшь, защищаешь, объясняешь.
current_p1_en:
Lawyer, Journalist, Sales Rep, PR Specialist. Your tool is the word. You persuade, sell, defend, explain.
This fits because you have a talent for communication. Most people can't articulate clearly; you do it professionally.
You may hear people don't get it: "how many words a day?". Thousands. And each one carries weight.
What's worth knowing: word professions also carry moral load. Sometimes you'll have to defend or sell something you don't like. Learn to separate. And remember — ethics matters more than short-term gain; reputation builds for years, falls in a day.

current_p1_ru: Chef, Musician, Artist, Photographer. Ты творишь не словами и не кодом — а другим материалом. Едой, звуком, краской, светом.
current_p1_en:
Chef, Musician, Artist, Photographer. You create not with words and not with code — with another material. Food, sound, paint, light.
Why it works: you have a deep connection to a specific medium. Words are too narrow for you; you need physical execution.
People sometimes don't believe: "you're a chef?". Yes. And every day is a performance.
What's worth knowing: these professions exhaust the body. Chef on feet 12 hours; musician touring; photographer hauling gear. Take care of the body. Without it the career is over.

current_p1_ru: Translator, Diplomat, Journalist, Teacher. Ты работаешь между мирами. Между языками, между странами, между разными аудиториями.
current_p1_en:
Translator, Diplomat, Journalist, Teacher. You work between worlds. Between languages, between countries, between different audiences.
It lands because you can see from different points. Most people live in one bubble; you move between several.
Some people are surprised: "what's your native language?". Several. And not one is fully native.
What's worth knowing: "between worlds" is also loneliness. You don't fully belong to any side. Learn to find "yours" — other in-betweeners. The community of bilinguals, diplomats, translators — that's your group.

current_p1_ru: Athlete, Chef, Doctor, Pilot. Твоя профессия требует физической формы. Не «офисная работа» — а активная, на ногах, с реальной нагрузкой.
current_p1_en:
Athlete, Chef, Doctor, Pilot. Your profession lives in the body too. Not "office work" — active, on your feet, with real load.
The logic is simple: you have body literacy. Many work only with the head; you understand the body is a tool that needs care.
You may hear people are surprised: "you're going down a mine?". No. My work just isn't at a desk.
What's worth knowing: physical professions have a shelf life. Athlete — to about 35; chef — to about 60; pilot — to 65. Plan the next stage. What will you do after? Better to ask at 30 than at 50.

current_p1_ru: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity. Ты используешь AI как помощника по тексту. Не для фотографий, не для видео; нужны слова — генерация, перевод, анализ, поиск.
current_p1_en:
ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity. You use AI as a text helper. Not for photos, not for video; you need words — generation, translation, analysis, search.
Why it works: your life runs through text. Documents, emails, notes. And AI cuts the work down dramatically.
Some people don't believe it: "so a neural net writes for you?". It does not write instead of you — it helps. Different thing.
What's worth knowing: text AI is a tool, not a replacement. If you stop writing yourself and just use it, the skill atrophies. Learn to alternate with your own writing.

current_p1_ru: Midjourney, Sora, DALL-E, Stable Diffusion. Ты живёшь в визуальном AI. Картинки, видео, концепт-арт — всё это можно генерить, и ты пользуешься.
current_p1_en:
Midjourney, Sora, DALL-E, Stable Diffusion. You live in the visual side of AI. Pictures, video, concept art — all of it can be generated, and you do.
It lands because you have visual thinking. Faster to show than to say; AI gives you the chance to create visuals without art school.
Some people object: "but it's not real art". Maybe. But it is a tool, and you use it as craft.
What's worth knowing: AI images can replace execution, but not the idea. If you have no idea of your own, AI won't make one. Learn to think first. Without an idea AI gives you generic output.

current_p1_ru: Copilot, Cursor, v0/Bolt, Claude. Ты используешь AI для работы с кодом или для проектирования продуктов. Это уже не «помощник»; это часть твоего рабочего инструментария.
current_p1_en:
Copilot, Cursor, v0/Bolt, Claude. You use AI for code or product design. This is no longer just a helper; it is part of your daily toolkit.
The logic is simple: your job needs code, and AI here isn't "trendy" — it really multiplies your speed.
Some people doubt: "but AI writes wrong code". Sometimes. My job is to fix that. AI handles the rough pass.
What's worth knowing: AI in code requires understanding code. If you're not a developer, AI won't make you one. Learn the fundamentals. Without them AI just speeds up your misunderstanding.

current_p1_ru: Suno, ElevenLabs, Runway, Sora. Ты используешь AI для звука и видео. Генерация музыки, клонирование голоса, монтаж — это твоё.
current_p1_en:
Suno, ElevenLabs, Runway, Sora. You use AI for sound and video. Music generation, voice cloning, editing — that's yours.
This fits because you have a creative request for media that AI now makes accessible. You can now make things that once required a studio.
Some people can't believe it: "you made the music yourself?". With AI, yes. And the help does not make it less yours.
What's worth knowing: AI music and voice are evolving fast but still detectable. Use as a draft, then polish. That makes the work yours, not AI-generated.

current_p1_ru: Copilot в Office, Notion AI, Perplexity в поиске, Gemini в Google. Ты не «идёшь к AI» — он встроен в твои привычные инструменты, и работает рядом с задачей.
current_p1_en:
Copilot in Office, Notion AI, Perplexity in search, Gemini in Google. You don't "go to AI" — it sits inside your familiar tools, working next to the task.
Why it works: you have a healthy relationship with AI. You don't summon it like a magical genie; you use it where it already shows up in your workflow.
Some people are surprised: "you use Notion AI?" You do. It writes summaries for you — and does it well.
What's worth knowing: built-in AI is often weaker than dedicated tools. ChatGPT is usually smarter than Notion AI; Claude smarter than Copilot. Sometimes step out of the convenience for the better tool.

current_p1_ru: Stable Diffusion, Cursor, v0/Bolt, Claude. Ты любишь инструменты, которые либо open source, либо очень узкоспецифичные. Тебе важен контроль и гибкость, а не «удобный сервис».
current_p1_en:
Stable Diffusion, Cursor, v0/Bolt, Claude. You like tools that are either open source or very specialized. Control and flexibility matter to you, not a "convenient service".
It lands because you have a geek's nature. You don't like depending on a cloud provider; you want to be able to run locally, modify, use without an account.
Some people don't get it: "but ChatGPT is more convenient". More convenient. And less free.
What's worth knowing: open source AI usually trails the best closed models. That's the price of freedom. Sometimes it's worth working with a 70%-as-good model for the flexibility.

current_p1_ru: YandexGPT, GigaChat, ChatGPT, Claude. Ты используешь и западные, и российские AI. Не из патриотизма, а из практики: разные модели — разные сильные стороны, и иногда местная знает контекст лучше глобальной.
current_p1_en:
YandexGPT, GigaChat, ChatGPT, Claude. You use both Western and Russian AI. Not out of patriotism, but practice: different models have different strengths, and sometimes the local one knows context better than the global one.
The logic is simple: you have a pragmatic approach. You are not loyal to one company; you use what works for the task.
Some people are surprised: "YandexGPT, really?". Yes. For Russian-language content it's often more accurate.
What's worth knowing: local AI is improving faster than it seems. Track updates. What was weak a year ago can be on par with global ones today.

category_name: Что ты чаще всего просишь у AI
current_p1_ru: Перевести, оформить, помочь принять решение, написать что-то простое. Ты не просишь у AI большое; ты используешь его для маленьких ежедневных задач, и от этого экономишь часы в неделю.
current_p1_en:
Translate, format, help me decide, write something simple. You don't only ask AI for big things; you use it for small daily tasks, and that saves you hours a week.
It lands because you don't have inflated expectations. Many people wait for AI miracles; you use it as a calculator for text. And that's enough.
Some people don't believe: "such a small thing, you can't do it yourself?". You can. But AI is faster.
What's worth knowing: everyday AI use is the most mature level. No hype, no expectations. Just a tool. Protect this attitude. Many people slowly start "believing in" AI and then get disappointed.

current_p1_ru: CS2, Valorant, Apex, Overwatch 2. Ты возвращаешься к шутерам ради соревнования. Не «постреляй ботов»; нужны живые противники, рейтинг, рост.
current_p1_en:
CS2, Valorant, Apex, Overwatch 2. You return to shooters for competition. Not shooting bots. You need live opponents, rank, growth.
Why it works: you have a sports instinct. In games you look for the same as in sport — measurable progress.
Some people don't get it: "why are you back there?" Because you're growing.
What's worth knowing: competitive shooters quickly become work. If you spend hours on "grinding" without enjoyment — it's no longer a game. Learn to notice when that line gets crossed.

current_p1_ru: Fortnite, PUBG, Apex, Valorant. Ты любишь массовые баталии. 100 игроков, один выживет. Каждая партия — отдельная история.
current_p1_en:
Fortnite, PUBG, Apex, Valorant. You love mass battles. A hundred players, one survives. Each match is its own story.
It lands because you crave adrenaline. In battle royale tension builds, and every winning moment is a small triumph.
You may hear people get tired of your stories: "another last-game story". But it really was interesting to you.
What's worth knowing: battle royale eats hours one match at a time. Each match 20-30 minutes, they glue into hours. Learn to set timers. Otherwise your day disappears.

current_p1_ru: Dota 2, League of Legends, Mobile Legends, Hearthstone. Ты в MOBA или в карточные стратегии. Глубокие игры, которые требуют годы для овладения.
current_p1_en:
Dota 2, League of Legends, Mobile Legends, Hearthstone. You're in MOBAs or card strategies. Deep games that take years to master.
The logic is simple: you have endurance. MOBA isn't "play for an hour"; it's years of accumulated knowledge.
People sometimes don't get it: "you have 5000 hours already". Yes, and still far from mastery.
What's worth knowing: MOBA communities are often toxic. Learn to tune out the chat. Otherwise the game you love becomes a stress source.

current_p1_ru: Witcher 3, Cyberpunk 2077, Baldur's Gate 3, Elden Ring. Ты возвращаешься в большие RPG за историями. Долгие, насыщенные, с серьёзным сюжетом.
current_p1_en:
Witcher 3, Cyberpunk 2077, Baldur's Gate 3, Elden Ring. You return to big RPGs for the stories. Long, dense, with serious plot.
This fits because you love to play like reading a book. Not "a quick session" — deep immersion.
Some people are surprised: "100 hours in one game?". A hundred, and still not enough for you. There are too many layers.
What's worth knowing: RPG epics take time, and many abandon mid-way. Be honest — do you have the resource for 80 hours? If not, postpone. Better in a year than half-finished.

current_p1_ru: GTA V, RDR 2, Cyberpunk, Witcher 3. Тебе нужны игры, в которых можно жить. Не «миссия за миссией» — а пространство, где ты сам(-а) выбираешь, что делать.
current_p1_en:
GTA V, RDR 2, Cyberpunk, Witcher 3. You need games where you can live. Not "mission after mission" — a space where you choose what to do.
Why it works: you love freedom. Linear games are a cage; open world is a field.
You may hear people don't get it: "you spent two hours on one square?". Two. There is life there.
What's worth knowing: open world can become an infinite trap. If you're constantly distracted by side quests, the main story passes you by. Learn to balance.

current_p1_ru: Stardew Valley, Animal Crossing, Sims 4, Terraria. Ты в играх ищешь покой. Не сражения; а ферму, дом, медленную жизнь.
current_p1_en:
Stardew Valley, Animal Crossing, Sims 4, Terraria. In games you look for peace. Not battles; a a farm, a home, a slow life.
It lands because your real life is already intense. In games you don't want more stress; you need the opposite.
People sometimes don't get it: "that's boring". Not boring — calm. Different things.
What's worth knowing: cozy games are great rest but no challenge. Learn to alternate. Only peace without trial is another form of burnout, through boredom.

current_p1_ru: Minecraft, Terraria, Roblox, Sims 4. Ты любишь, когда игра даёт инструменты, а не цель. Что строить, во что превратить мир — твой выбор.
current_p1_en:
Minecraft, Terraria, Roblox, Sims 4. You love when a game gives tools, not goals. What to build, what to turn the world into — your choice.
The logic is simple: you have a creative streak. Going through someone else's plot isn't enough; you need to create your own.
Some people are surprised: "you play Roblox?". Roblox. Everyone is there now, and among them are brilliant creators.
What's worth knowing: sandboxes can become time-sinks. Without goals you can play forever and finish nothing. Learn to set yourself tasks. Otherwise the game becomes idleness.

current_p1_ru: Hollow Knight, Elden Ring, Stray, Baldur's Gate 3. Ты любишь сложные одиночные игры с глубиной. Не «лёгкое прохождение»; нужно, чтобы поломали голову.
current_p1_en:
Hollow Knight, Elden Ring, Stray, Baldur's Gate 3. You love hard solo games with depth. Not "easy clearance"; you want it to break your head.
This fits because you have patience for the difficult. Most people don't last; you get pleasure precisely from overcoming.
You may hear people look at you like a masochist. Not a masochist — you just have a different threshold.
What's worth knowing: Souls games can become an obsession. If you're stuck on one and trying every evening, doing nothing else — that's no longer love, it's stubbornness. Sometimes a pause is needed.

current_p1_ru: Hearthstone, Clash Royale, Brawl Stars, Mobile Legends. Ты любишь короткие сессии. Карточки, мобильные стратегии, мгновенные матчи.
current_p1_en:
Hearthstone, Clash Royale, Brawl Stars, Mobile Legends. You love short sessions. Card games, mobile strategies, instant matches.
Why it works: your time is limited. 3 minutes in line, in a café, in the bathroom — everywhere you can play. And you do.
People sometimes accuse: "you're always on your phone". Not always — short sessions. Different things.
What's worth knowing: "short sessions" accumulate. Ten three-minute ones is half an hour a day. Learn to notice when that line gets crossed. Sometimes worth knowing how much you actually play.

current_p1_ru: WoW, Path of Exile, Genshin Impact, Honkai Star Rail. Ты живёшь в MMO. Не «играешь» — постоянно с друзьями в одном виртуальном мире, и этот мир для тебя реальная социальная среда.
current_p1_en:
WoW, Path of Exile, Genshin Impact, Honkai Star Rail. You live in MMOs. Not "play" — constantly with friends in one virtual world, and that world is a real social environment for you.
It lands because you have real friends there. MMO isn't a game, it's a meeting territory.
Some people don't get it: "you have friends from a game?". Yes. And these are real friends, just living in another country.
What's worth knowing: MMOs eat enormous hours. And interest fades, friends remain — but the game is no longer interesting. Learn to separate "playing this" from "talking to these people". If only the friendship — you can move it elsewhere.

current_p1_ru: Among Us, Rocket League, Brawl Stars, Fortnite. Ты любишь играть с друзьями. Не «соло гриндить»; а смех в дискорде, и абсурдная ситуация в каждой партии.
current_p1_en:
Among Us, Rocket League, Brawl Stars, Fortnite. You love playing with friends. Not "solo grind"; laughter in Discord, and an absurd situation in every match.
The logic is simple: for you the game is social glue. You don't "escape into a virtual world"; you play to be with friends more vividly.
You may hear people are surprised: "you play Among Us?". Yes. And in the evening with friends, it still works. It's the best communication possible.
What's worth knowing: social games work when you have someone to play with. Without friends they quickly become uninteresting. Learn to value this infrastructure of friendship.
